name: Structural Marxism
summary: Structural Marxism, founded by Louis Althusser and developed by Nicos Poulantzas and Etienne Balibar, reads Marx as a scientist of social structures rather than a humanist of alienated human essence. Society is a structured whole of economic, political and ideological levels, with the economy determining only in the last instance, and individuals are bearers of structures constituted as subjects by ideology. It keeps the communist aim and class struggle but rejects humanism, economism and teleological history.
scope: The Althusserian school of the 1960s-70s (For Marx, Reading Capital, Ideology and Ideological State Apparatuses) with Poulantzas on the capitalist state and Balibar on modes of production. Positions on the party and democracy follow Althusser's late essays within the French Communist Party tradition; it excludes Analytical, Frankfurt and humanist Marxism, and Maoist or anthropological structural-Marxist offshoots.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Althusser's school-and-state analysis treats welfare provision as a contested terrain within the apparatuses; a Marxist party of the left backs universal public health care, though not as the goal.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not discussed by the school; as a PCF-aligned communist tradition it supports gains for wage earners, inferred from its class-struggle stance, while seeing wage reform as reformist.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Structural Marxism takes capitalist commodity relations as the object of critique (Capital) and sees market allocation as the mechanism of exploitation.

public-ownership.rationale: Abolishing private ownership of the means of production is the Marxist aim the school inherits; public ownership of major industry follows from that.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not a theme of the school; a communist adherent would support it as a redistributive step while holding that taxation does not alter relations of production.

unions-good.rationale: Althusser lists trade unions among the ISAs but treats them as sites of class struggle where the exploited can resist, so adherents back them while stressing their ambiguity.

property-fundamental.rationale: Reproduction of the relations of production is Althusser's object of critique; private ownership of the means of production is what must be overthrown.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: regulation is a reform of capitalism, which adherents support tactically but regard as insufficient.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cutting welfare is a class-war move against workers; the school's class analysis opposes it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective ownership of production is the communist aim, though the school stresses the state and party as agents, so workers' co-ops specifically are a milder fit.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: Althusser sees the repressive apparatus as an organ of class rule that must be transformed, so adherents distrust expanded policing powers.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the French left's usual libertarian-on-morals stance, with low confidence.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The school did not address it; adherents could see it as bourgeois legality or as protection of the oppressed.

strong-leader.rationale: Althusser condemned the Stalinist cult of personality and argued for mass democracy and party discussion.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is an instrument of class rule that should eventually wither away, but Althusser insists it is needed in the transition, so not simply harmful now.

limit-guns.rationale: No treatment in the school; adherents split between disarming and arming-the-people traditions.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and army are the Repressive State Apparatus of the ruling class, so adherents oppose strengthening them.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist-aligned views split between abolition as exploitation and decriminalisation.

decide-locally.rationale: Inferred: the school analyses the national state and centralised party; localism is not part of its program.

rehabilitation.rationale: Prisons are part of the repressive apparatus; adherents would favour rehabilitation over punishment but the school said little.

traditional-family.rationale: The family is listed as an Ideological State Apparatus that reproduces ideology, not a foundation to be defended.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by the school; inferred from the progressive French left of the 1960s-70s.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left's general support for reproductive rights.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion, like the Church, is an ISA that reproduces the ruling ideology; a larger public role is opposed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a central topic; the Marxist left supports it in principle but frames oppression through class.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Human nature has no fixed essence and individuals are produced as subjects through ideology, which suggests gender is socially formed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ideology is treated as a vehicle for reproducing class relations, so preserving traditions is not a value for the school.

gradual-change.rationale: Revolution as ruptural unity of contradictions is central; deference to existing institutions is rejected, though Althusser allows peaceful routes.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not discussed; internationalist communist tradition opposes restriction, inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not discussed; adherents were wary of bourgeois international bodies yet internationalist.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from critique of capitalism; the school did not discuss trade policy directly.

nation-first.rationale: Marxist internationalism opposes placing national interests over cooperation among peoples.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism; Western intervention is viewed as imperial power.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalist but the school never took a position on borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Not discussed; the school focuses on relations of production, and it did not endorse degrowth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from left politics, with low confidence.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Social problems are rooted in relations of production, not technology; Althusser attacked technocratic and economistic readings.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is not discussed by the school and no principle of structural analysis bears on it; the French communist milieu was historically pro-nuclear while others dissented.

revolution-justified.rationale: Althusser treats revolution as the rupture of accumulated contradictions, though he accepts that the form depends on the balance of forces.

experts-over-public.rationale: Althusser privileges scientific theory but under party and mass control; an elite of experts against the public is not his position.

central-planning.rationale: Socialist planned economy is the Marxist-Leninist aim, though Althusser's own stress was theoretical, not economic.

socialized-markets.rationale: Commodity relations are what Capital analyses as exploitative; market socialism is not the aim.

land-value-tax.rationale: A Georgist tax is a bourgeois reform and not part of the school's program.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: curbing inheritance accumulation is consistent with Marxist aims but not a stated theme.

basic-income.rationale: Not discussed; adherents split between seeing it as a gain and as a palliative within capitalism.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The school never addressed trade policy, and Marxists have split between seeing tariffs as protecting workers and as a bourgeois nationalist tool.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Planning investment under working-class state power is the socialist aim.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Marxism opposes small private property in the means of production as a basis for society and seeks socialisation.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolition of wage labour and commodity production is the long-run communist aim, as in Capital.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Marxists want finance brought under public control rather than left to the market, so handing money to the market is the opposite of the aim.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Class collaboration through state bodies is opposed in favour of class struggle.

one-party-rule.rationale: Althusser moved away from Soviet one-party models, called for mass democracy, and criticised the PCF's authoritarianism, while keeping a vanguard role for the party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Monarchy is a feudal form of class rule rejected by the Marxist tradition.

democracy-best.rationale: In 1977 Althusser said socialism must be reached democratically through universal suffrage, but he treated bourgeois democracy as class rule.

direct-votes.rationale: The school did not take up direct democracy; mass democracy is its theme but its form unspecified.

workers-councils.rationale: Althusser's mass democracy suggests mass organs, but he did not endorse councils explicitly.

right-to-secede.rationale: Lenin defended national self-determination, but Althusser and the school took no position on regional secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rejects any fixed human essence or natural hierarchy; ideology constructs subjects.

political-violence-never.rationale: Althusser says Marx and Lenin never excluded violence where the bourgeoisie imposes it.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from Marxist internationalism, which sees war between states as a product of capitalist rivalry rather than a source of virtue.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion is an ISA; separating it from the state is consistent with secular French left-wing views.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion is an ideological apparatus of class rule, so adherents reject scripture as basis of law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts and army belong to the state apparatus; privatizing them would hand them directly to capital.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from the anti-militarist, internationalist communist tradition; the PCF itself backed the French deterrent, so not stronger.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The school treats ideology as socially constructed and rejects ethnic essentialism; Balibar later wrote against race.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Althusser's later work makes class struggle the motor of history, as the Wikipedia summary of the school records.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Communist distribution by need entails strong equality, though the school did not discuss the issue directly.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the anti-colonial stance of the Marxist left, with low confidence.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the left's anti-imperialism and Marx's critique of colonial extraction.

civilizational-union.rationale: Marxist internationalism is class-based, not civilizational.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Rejects individualism; individuals are bearers of structures, and bourgeois ideology constructs the self-interested subject.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; rejects individual-rights humanism as ideology but does not subordinate rights to community duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The school analyses relations of production, not environmental ethics, so it supplies no basis for the answer.

limit-population.rationale: Marxists traditionally reject Malthusian explanations; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Capitalism developed the productive forces; the school rejects the anti-industrial view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Productive forces matter, but the school stresses that relations of production decide their social effect, so it neither welcomes nor resists disruption as such.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanism is outside the school's concerns, and its anti-humanism does not settle it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: technocratic rule conflicts with mass democracy under class control.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not discussed; Marxists could favour either privacy against the repressive apparatus or state security.

restore-past-order.rationale: History has no direction to restore, and the school opposes reactionary politics.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Ideology is unavoidable and shapes all practice, so claiming to be non-ideological is itself ideological.

direct-action.rationale: Althusser favours a mix of mass politics and elections; the school has no stated position on direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rejects strict prefigurative politics; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Marxism sees progress through modes of production; foraging is not a goal.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Communism implies overcoming the division of labour, but Althusser criticised the humanist young-Marx framing in which this is formulated.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The communist principle from each according to ability, to each according to need is the long-run aim.

production-for-use.rationale: Replacing commodity production by production for need is the communist aim.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Reproduction of labour power and relations of production, per Althusser, rests on exploitation of wage labour as analysed in Capital.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Althusser argued the concept cannot be dropped by decision, yet tied it to mass democracy and opposed Stalinist dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Not discussed; collectivisation is associated with Soviet practice that Althusser criticised.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred from classical Marxist-Leninist theory of imperialism, which the school largely inherits.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anti-capitalist tradition treats taxation as legitimate public revenue.

harm-principle.rationale: A liberal principle of limits on the state; the school sees the state as class apparatus and offers no endorsement or rejection of this rule.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rejects the liberal individual as ideological construct and treats subjects as products of structures.

conscription.rationale: Marxists have both backed citizen armies and opposed militarism; the school took no position.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Liberal-libertarian idea alien to the school's class analysis.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers contradicts its class view of the state.

positive-liberty.rationale: Freedom needs material conditions in Marxist thought; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Schools and media are ISAs that serve the ruling class, not independent power holders.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Rejects fixed essences and biological determination of social difference.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation is rejected in favour of class politics.

total-state.rationale: Althusser condemned Stalinist state excesses and called for state withering.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nationalist narratives of decadence and rebirth are ideological forms the school would analyse, not endorse; history has no subject or telos for it.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Expansion is read as imperialism in the Marxist-Leninist tradition the school stems from.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal fealty is a pre-capitalist mode of rule; adherents regard it as an ideological form to be overcome.

bound-labor.rationale: Feudal servitude is a pre-capitalist exploitation form rejected.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Althusser held that ideology is pervasive but that science, including historical materialism, produces objective knowledge through epistemological breaks.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral and humanist universals are treated as ideology, not knowledge.

single-common-good.rationale: Althusser treats politics as class struggle and the appeal to a common good as ideology that conceals class interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The school did not address Zionism and Marxists are divided on it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed by the school; no principle decides the issue for it.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a topic the school addressed.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control of the economy by workers fits socialist aims.

school-vouchers.rationale: The school is the dominant ISA; privatising choice is opposed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Austerity-minded fiscal rules serve capital, so an adherent would resist them, though the school itself said little on macroeconomics.

economic-freedom.rationale: The claim that political freedom depends on market freedom is a liberal ideology that the school rejects.

rule-by-example.rationale: Moral example as a basis of rule is an idealist view; the school looks to structures and class power rather than the virtue of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Leninist support for self-determination is not developed by the school.

force-without-un.rationale: Anti-imperialist inference; unilateral force abroad is read as great-power domination.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Science versus ideology is central, though Althusser stresses theoretical practice more than reason in the Enlightenment sense.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Internationalist class politics sees workers as one class regardless of nationality, so excluding immigrants is rejected.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Conditional welfare is typically opposed by the left; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Althusser holds the ISAs and the state sit within a class struggle in which classes are opposed, so partnership between employers and workers conceals exploitation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not discussed; a Marxist would not favour destroying cultural institutions, which are sites of struggle rather than obstacles.

dominated-front.rationale: Third-worldist fronts were a Maoist theme, not part of the school itself.

workers-nation.rationale: Marxism organises workers internationally rather than nationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The family is an ISA reproducing gender roles, which the school criticises.

ban-interest.rationale: Marx explained interest as a form of surplus value; legal prohibition is not the school's remedy, which is socialisation of finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Rejects racial essences and treats such categories as ideological constructions that serve class domination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Althusser sees apparatuses as organs of class rule, though structuralists reject a crude instrumentalism.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not addressed; no principle of the school decides it.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from internationalism; the school does not treat national culture as something immigrants must adopt.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theories about deliberate plots conflict with structural analysis of outcomes as products of structures, not of intentions.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems were not treated by the school.

national-mission.rationale: Messianic nationalism is an ideology that interpellates subjects; adherents reject it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Later adherents such as Mitchell linked it to Althusserian ideology theory, but Althusser prioritised class.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Structural analysis attributes outcomes to class structure rather than individual corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics rests on biological essence of the person, which the anti-humanist school treats as ideological, and Marxists opposed it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Althusser condemned the Stalinist repression and supported accountability, inferred for other states.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The school seeks transformation of the state and the economy, not a minimal state protecting property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial essentialism is rejected as ideology.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Humanist egalitarianism is called ideological, though adherents politically support equality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed by the school; Althusser criticised Soviet practice but did not engage the debate.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed by the school, and Marxists are divided over settler colonial framing.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; secular French leftism suggests support, but the school itself is silent.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Althusser sees religion as ideology, but the French secular left defended freedom of conscience, so restriction is rejected on low confidence.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; a religious-based ban is contrary to secular materialism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion is an ISA; removing it from state schools fits the French left's secular stance.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Althusser calls for the state to wither away and criticised Soviet statism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Consent is liberal contract language; Althusser's ISA analysis suggests consent is manufactured by ideology, so adherents are split on this principle.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aim not addressed by the school.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and class solidarity across ethnic lines.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Rejects liberal absolutism on force; revolution may require violence.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Class struggle, not social Darwinian competition, drives history.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; PCF was itself subject to bans in the past, inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican notion not addressed in the school; although domination is a concern, it is framed as class power.

separated-powers.rationale: The school stresses unity of class power within the state, so separation is not a priority.

vanguard-party.rationale: Althusser wanted the party to be one step ahead of the masses, while also demanding democratic reform within it.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The school is a class-based critique siding with the exploited, so first priority to the poor is a natural inference but not a stated point.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not discussed; privatisation of public housing is opposed on the left.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Althusser counts unions as ISAs in which the exploited can resist, so restrictions on strikes attack working-class power.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxists traditionally reject Malthusian explanation and ground poverty in relations of production.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Treats ethnic essentialism as ideology; cohesion problems are explained by class relations.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed by the school.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Althusser criticised Soviet-style repression and legal arbitrariness, so he would reject wide emergency powers, though not absolutely.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A planned-economy inference: setting prices of necessities is consistent with socialist aims, though not a stated position.

party-controls-media.rationale: Althusser rejected Stalinist control and favoured open discussion within the party.

party-commands-army.rationale: Althusser favoured party leadership of the masses but never discussed army command, and he criticised Soviet statism.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Marx praised the Paris Commune's low pay for officials, a precedent for the tradition, but the school did not discuss it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Althusser accepted democratic centralism but wanted it reformed and opposed organised tendencies.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The PCF opposed the European Community in this period while internationalism is generally welcomed, so the school offers no clear answer.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential concentration of power conflicts with mass democracy, but the school took no explicit stand.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Church is an ISA; a hierarchical church seems a typical ideological apparatus, but the statement concerns internal church governance, which adherents do not care about.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religion is an ideological apparatus, and rule by clerics opposes the school's secularism.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin's revolutionary defeatism, the tradition's classic position, but Althusser did not discuss it, so low confidence.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Althusser opposed Stalinist cultural controls; moral censorship is rejected.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not discussed; personalist rule is disfavoured.

recall-officials.rationale: Mass democracy implies accountable representatives, though recall as such is not discussed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The PCF opposed NATO integration, but Althusser did not discuss alliances, so it is neutral.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Universal private home ownership expands private property, which the school opposes; housing is better socialised.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Marxist tradition supports armed workers in revolution, but the school never took this up.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Romanticising rural life is a bourgeois ideology; Marx noted the idiocy of rural life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Althusser was himself a professor and favoured theory as part of politics.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Schools are ISAs, and adherents want them progressive rather than reproducing traditional gender ideology; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious doctrine in public schools is the Church's ideological influence that Althusser critiques, and adherents prize science.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Marxists split between seeing pornography as exploitation and opposing censorship.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based citizenship rests on ethnic essence; the school rejects such essentialism.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from the left's opposition to cultural domination, but not discussed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; adherents could see exemptions as protecting the vulnerable or as entrenching ideology.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A liberal Millian ideal; the school treats individuals as products of structures, and there is no stance.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism, not stated by the school.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist view that formal independence leaves economic dependence; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not discussed; Althusser accepted universal suffrage but did not address constitutional procedure.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Althusser condemned Stalinist repression and insisted socialism requires democracy.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid is seen as inadequate, though adherents support transfers; split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The PCF supported the French deterrent, others did not; no school position.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not discussed; he would regard presidentialism with suspicion.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Independent central banks insulate capital from democratic control, so adherents would oppose them, though the school did not address the point.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The school never discussed territorial disputes, and class internationalism offers no clear answer on exchanging land for peace.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Private property in means of production is to be socialised, so justification only by common good fits, though it is a moralised wording.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Althusser criticised Stalinism but did not call the USSR state capitalist; the PCF view was the opposite.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliances not discussed; the PCF was suspicious of NATO.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed by the school, though anti-imperialism suggests support.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Church is an ISA; curbing it is consistent with French secular left.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ceremonial heads of state are outside the school's concerns, and nothing in its theory decides whether one should stand above party.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Ideology that interpellates subjects is analysed critically; sacred rulers are rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A flat rate is regressive in effect and favours the rich; the left opposes it.

character-from-environment.rationale: No human essence; individuals are formed by social structures and ideology.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule above law is absolutist; Althusser's Marxism opposes arbitrary power while treating bourgeois law as class form.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is far from the school's subject matter, and its structural method gives no verdict on it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mixed constitution is a classical idea for balancing classes; the school regards class as conflict, so it would be rejected.

leader-cult.rationale: Althusser criticised the cult of personality as Stalinist distortion.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Althusser says class struggle continues under socialism in transformed forms; the claim that party leaders may be in a bourgeois position is a Maoist addition, so milder.

land-redistribution.rationale: Marxist-Leninist agrarian programmes favoured it, though Althusser did not discuss land reform.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and rights of the displaced, low confidence.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Ethnic irredentism is nationalist ideology that the school rejects.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religion is an ideological apparatus whose coercion adherents oppose, and the secular left defends freedom of conscience.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsion tied to patriarchal ideology is rejected.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed by the school; communists split on EU monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic political unity rests on ethnic essence, not on class.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed by the school; Austro-Marxists proposed it while Lenin opposed it.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Economy is determinant only in the last instance, with relative autonomy of politics and ideology.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust seeks to restore competition, a liberal aim, whereas the school seeks to supersede capitalist markets.

no-bailouts.rationale: Neither bailing out capital nor letting workers bear failures is a position the school took.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Courts are part of the state apparatus; the school saw no value in majoritarian absolutism per se, but did not discuss it.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the left's support for gender equality.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic imperial blocs are a fascist or mercantilist idea, not Marxist.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred as a pro-worker measure within capitalism.

moral-incentives.rationale: Althusser criticised humanist moralism; economism also rejected.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Revolution arises from condensed contradictions, not from voluntarism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Aristocratic privilege is a feudal class form; Marxists want it abolished along with class privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: School history curricula are an ISA that reproduces ideology, and adherents resist nationalistic framing.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial tutelage is imperialism and treated as an ideological cover for exploitation.

patriotic-education.rationale: Schools reproduce ideology; adherents criticise patriotic indoctrination.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; the left generally supports such preferences, with mixed class views.

public-money-creation.rationale: Public control of finance accords with socialist aims.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalism's contradictions can condense into crisis, as the school's concept of overdetermination holds, though it also stressed adaptation by the state.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Neo-imperial influence is rejected as imperialism.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency delinking is Amin's theory, not Althusser's.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed by the school; Marxists are divided on it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The left rejects discrimination in the market on principle.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Bourgeois legal form; adherents have no firm stance.

elective-rulers.rationale: Althusser accepts universal suffrage as the democratic route to socialism, and monarchy is a feudal form, so electing rulers fits, though the question of the political nation is not his.

minority-veto.rationale: Unanimity rules would let a single member block collective decisions; Marxist class politics rejects that.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Althusser accepts revolution when the bourgeoisie imposes violence, so resisting rulers who break constitutional trust is compatible, though he views bourgeois legality as class rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Althusser favoured democratic route via universal suffrage but saw parliament as bourgeois.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is outside the school's concerns.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is outside the school's concerns.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aristocratic paternalism is an ideology that masks class domination, and adherents want structural change, not benevolence.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The school is explicitly about political practice and class struggle, so withdrawal from politics is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Media and cultural ISAs reproduce the relations of production.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: ISAs secure ideological consent behind the protection of repression; both.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist imperialism theory; Balibar worked on modes of production in colonial contexts.

native-born-offices.rationale: Birth-based office restriction rests on national essence, contrary to internationalist class politics.

party-own-road.rationale: Althusser supported French road to socialism and opposed Soviet model imposed on parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not discussed in the school.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is nationalist, and an internationalist adherent would reject it.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; anti-colonial sympathies are balanced by class-first politics.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Communist parties defined themselves partly through antifascism, an inference for the school.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Althusser condemned Stalinism but would reject equating Marxism with fascism as ideological.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxist historiography treats slavery as the central contradiction of the antebellum social formation.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monuments are part of ideological apparatuses; adherents would not seek their preservation, though the school did not discuss it.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; class analysis does not decide it.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Civilizational relativism is not a Marxist position; modes of production, not civilizations, structure societies.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army is a repressive state apparatus of the ruling class, so a political guardian role is rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: Juliet Mitchell's Althusserian feminism took reproductive labour seriously; this is an inference.

filial-duty.rationale: The family is an ISA reproducing ideology; lifelong duty as moral norm is not endorsed.

office-by-exam.rationale: Meritocratic exam rule is a Confucian-bureaucratic ideal, while mass democracy is the school's aim.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not addressed; adherents could favour it as anti-imperial or reject economic nationalism.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the left's critique of the family as ideological apparatus.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Paris Commune model recognised by Marx; Althusser's mass democracy is compatible, though not stated.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatised pensions turn social insurance into capital markets; the left opposes it.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal land tenure is not discussed in the school, though Balibar's modes-of-production work touched pre-capitalist tenure without prescribing it.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed, though Marxists regard parliament as only one terrain.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not taken up by the school, and Marxists have differed on a common state language versus minority rights.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Restrictions on foreign ownership are not discussed; adherents might see them as anti-imperialist or as nationalist.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal doctrine on indirect discrimination is not addressed, though structural analysis of outcomes might lean toward it, so left neutral.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumer culture is a capitalist ideological form; inferred rather than stated.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert intervention is read as imperialism.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Althusser criticised Soviet practice and the Stalinist model; invading allies to hold them in a bloc is imperial.

corporate-influence.rationale: The state apparatus is organised around the interests of capital, and lobbying is an expression of that.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; adherents could see it as anti-imperialist or authoritarian.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; pronatalism is usually nationalist.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local residency limits on property purchase are not discussed by the school and adherents could read them as anti-speculation or as exclusionary.

job-guarantee.rationale: Full employment is a long-standing left aim, an inference.

democratic-peace.rationale: Marxists tie war to imperialist competition among capitalist democracies, so spreading democracy as peace is not accepted.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Law is class form but Althusser did not state a moral duty position.

non-intervention.rationale: Althusser accepted revolutions made by forces; non-interference as absolute is not stated.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed; the Marxist-Leninist tradition favours industrial organisation but the school did not discuss it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories oppose structural analysis, which is the school's defining method of explaining social events by structures, not plots.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Family as ISA is critiqued, but abolition of legal marriage is not proposed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not a stated position; democratic transparency inferred from his call for open debate in the party.

local-production.rationale: Localism is not part of the school.

informal-organisation.rationale: Althusser insisted on party organisation and democratic centralism reformed, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The school has no doctrine on precedence between national and international law, and class-based internationalism points both ways.

religious-nation.rationale: Religion is an ISA; defining nation by it is opposed.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary hierarchy is an imperial relation the school rejects.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; the left favours redistribution between regions but the school did not take up the point.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxist distinction between personal and productive property.

defeat-communism.rationale: The statement targets the adherents' own tradition, whose goal is communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Marketisation of public services is resisted by the left, an inference.

religion-illusion.rationale: Ideology consoles; Althusser treats religion as an ideological apparatus, but ideology is permanent rather than fading, hence not strongly.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marx's view that capitalism developed productive forces, accepted by Althusser's reading of Capital.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist feminism ties women's subordination to relations of production, though Althusserians stressed ideology and family too.

socialized-care.rationale: Marxist tradition favours socialising housework, inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty rights of nations within a state are not discussed by the school and nothing in its theory settles them.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small utopian communes are rejected by Marxism in favour of transforming the whole structure.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ethnic colonisation of minority regions is rejected as nationalism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Adherents hold communism as their aim, so a third course is rejected.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist claims are ideologies.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial is a falsification of history incompatible with scientific Marxism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not discussed by the school; Althusser's own milieu was progressive, so inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Althusser criticised Stalinist repression and demanded internal party freedom of discussion.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Religious ideology should not be enforced by the state.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonialism is read as imperial exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religion as political duty is not part of the school, though anti-imperialist resistance might be sympathised.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Rejects theocratic legitimacy as an ideological apparatus.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Althusser called for mass democracy as the form of proletarian rule.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Althusserian scholars spoke of overdetermination of multiple contradictions, but the statement is intersectionality, not the school's text.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from French left secularism.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Althusser's whole work presupposes a class struggle that makes the left-right division fundamental.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation belongs to the young Marx's humanist problematic, which Althusser rejected as ideology.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Althusser analyses God as the central Subject of an ideological apparatus, not a source of legitimate authority.

social-market-economy.rationale: Social market economy preserves capitalism; adherents seek its supersession.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The repressive apparatus is to be transformed, but abolition of armed forces is not stated.

rich-first.rationale: Differentiated development is a Deng-style view the school does not hold.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; the PCF belonged to the Soviet-aligned camp, while Althusser criticised it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary leadership contradicts mass democracy and is a feudal form.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist credit is a Proudhonian approach that Marxists criticise.

property-franchise.rationale: Class-based franchise is bourgeois class rule; the school endorses universal suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not part of the school.

reification.rationale: Reification is a Lukacsian Hegelian-Marxist concept the school rejected.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Media are ISAs under ruling-class control, so formal freedoms mean little.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule-of-law formalism is a legal form of the bourgeois state, but nothing specific stated.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial essence is ideology, and the school supports universal suffrage.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation was not a topic in the 1960s-70s texts, though mass democracy is compatible with it; left neutral.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency is consistent with mass democracy.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religious control over family life is the ideological apparatus the school criticises.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition-based assemblies are not discussed, and Althusser's mass democracy was organised through parties and unions instead.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Althusser early tried reconciling Christianity and Marxism but later abandoned it; the school has no position on reform of doctrine.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not discussed by the school; as the army is a repressive apparatus adherents may not care, but anti-discrimination is inferred from the left milieu.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Althusser says ideology is permanent in all societies, so promoting atheism would replace one ideology with another; also state coercion is criticised.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Repressive apparatus is to be transformed, but not abolished before the state withers.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational arrangements are not addressed, and a class-first view treats ethnic divisions as ideological rather than a basis for institutions.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Philanthropy reproduces inequality, so adherents prefer public provision.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed by the school and are neither required nor opposed by its theory of the state.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid delegation is not addressed by the school, though accountable delegates fit mass democracy loosely.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction-risk prioritisation is not part of the school's concerns and no principle of structural Marxism decides it.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Internationalist class politics gives no weight to long waiting periods for citizenship.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Rejects hierarchy of civilizations, though Althusser also rejected relativist humanism.

death-penalty.rationale: The repressive apparatus is an instrument of class rule, and the French left opposed capital punishment, though Marxists have not rejected it absolutely.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: Marxist politics extends rights to workers regardless of origin, but Althusser's sources do not address it.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: a communist-party Marxist would back housing regulation as a reform, though the sources do not discuss rent.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: Marxism treats intellectual property as bourgeois property relations, though the school did not address patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Althusser's ideological state apparatus analysis treats youth organisations of this kind as instruments of the dominant ideology.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; communist parties of the period split on nuclear weapons, and the school has no stated position.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: the French Communist Party tradition opposed foreign bases as imperialism, though the sources do not discuss it.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: left Marxists back recognition of historical crimes, but the school did not discuss it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The core Marxist analysis of capitalist relations of production holds that property ownership extracts surplus from labour, as Althusser's Marxism reads Capital.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: Marxism accepts revolutionary and defensive violence, and Althusser rejects moralism; not directly discussed.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Althusser's anti-humanist, anti-teleological reading of history rejects national essences, treating identity as produced by ideological apparatuses.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: Althusser's account of subjects constituted by ideology fits constructionism, but the school did not address sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: the theory of subjects constituted by ideology fits rejecting fixed categories, though not discussed for feminism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Althusser treated nationalism and religious veneration as ideology, so he would reject honouring martyrs as saints.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The school treats politics as class struggle in structures and religion as an ideological apparatus, not as a struggle of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: Marxism is internationalist and rejects nationalist homeland politics; not discussed directly.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: Marxist politics puts class struggle and the state first, with culture as a superstructure.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: Althusser analysed religion as an ideological apparatus and would not require a male God, but did not address it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; the school analyses religion as ideology rather than judging texts by a feminist standard.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Marxist internationalism rejects economic dominance by a national majority; class, not nation, divides the economy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: Marxist internationalism rejects ethnic territorial units, though not discussed.

independent-unions.rationale: Althusser counted trade unions among the ideological state apparatuses, yet the PCF-aligned tradition worked with allied unions, so adherents are not clearly for or against independence.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Althusser's late writing defended the dictatorship of the proletariat and the democratic road, which requires the working class to hold real power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: A communist school would favour public provision of essentials, but it did not address local services specifically; inferred from its socialist aim.

second-chamber.rationale: Its analysis of parliament as part of the bourgeois state suggests little support for an additional chamber, inferred from the state theory.

municipal-property.rationale: The school aims at socialisation of the means of production under working-class state power, not municipal ownership; inferred from its programme.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; its focus on state and party apparatuses points away from confederal localism.

family-wage.rationale: Althusser treated the family as an ideological apparatus reproducing relations of production, so a family wage is unlikely to be endorsed.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed by the school; no clear position can be inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed by the school; no clear position can be inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Althusser's anti-humanism treats the human essence as ideology and individuals as bearers of structures, so a person as an end in himself is rejected.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Althusser treated religion as an ideological state apparatus and the human essence as ideology, rejecting a spiritual nature as a basis for politics.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The school places class above race as the structuring contradiction, so organising by racial interest is inferred to be rejected.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from its class-first analysis and its view of identities as ideological constructs.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist views on war depend on its class character.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from the school's stress on class structure over national identity; Poulantzas treats the nation as a capitalist state form.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the class analysis, which treats religious divisions as ideological rather than a basis of representation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred; the school explains politics through class structures, not foreign conspiracies.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the communist aim; Althusser's critique of the school as an ideological apparatus concerns its role, not tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred; the school looks to structural change of relations of production rather than price instruments within capitalism.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the communist aim of a lasting, sustainable society; not stated by the school.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from Althusser's anti-essentialism, which rejects claims that groups hold inherent shared values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the French Communist Party's peace line in the tradition Althusser worked within.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the communist aim of state direction of the economy against capital.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Althusser treats the army and police as the repressive state apparatus of the ruling class, so an armed-state monopoly is a feature of class rule, but he never discussed disarming other groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Althusser's late writing opposes imperialist war within the communist tradition, which suggests sympathy for refusal, but the school did not address soldiers' disobedience directly.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Althusser sees trade unions as a site of class struggle in the party's orbit and a Marxist party backs union bargaining, though the school regards it as insufficient for revolution.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are a reformist welfare device that the school would treat as ambiguous, accommodating capitalism while aiding workers, and the sources never discuss them.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules that bind governments fit capital's interest in a state that is relatively autonomous but class-bound; the school would oppose them as constraints on workers' gains, inferred from Poulantzas.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The communist tradition around Althusser opposed imperialism and unequal exchange, so reordering the world economy for developing countries is inferred as agreeable, though not a school theme.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Althusser's ISA essay argues the state apparatus serves the ruling class and must be destroyed in the transition, though the school, via Poulantzas, favoured transforming it by a long struggle.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Althusser's science of history rejects utopian blueprints in favour of the communist aim, but a fixed social-formation analysis conflicts with a no-blueprint pluralism of systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The school treats nature as a material base of production in a mode of production, not as capital to be valued by the economy, so pricing ecosystems is inferred as a capitalist move.

sacred-nation.rationale: Althusser treats the nation as an ideological formation that constitutes subjects, so a sacred nation that gives lives meaning is exactly the ideology the school aims to expose.

student-debt-relief.rationale: A left Marxist party would back student debt relief as lessening the burden on workers, though it is a reform and the sources do not discuss it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Althusser did not take up internal colonialism, and Poulantzas' analysis of the state concerns class structure more than regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Althusser's Marxism and Humanism denies any fixed human essence, holding that humanist talk of a human nature is ideological and that people are produced as subjects by structures.

public-service-media.rationale: A Marxist party would back public media against commercial control, though Althusser regarded media as an ideological apparatus of the state that is never free of class influence.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Althusser treats religion as an ideological state apparatus that interpellates subjects, not as a vehicle of truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred: a Marxist left supports state protection of small producers within a transition programme, though the school did not discuss agriculture.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The French Communist Party accepted the national deterrent in the 1970s while opposing nuclear imperialism, and Althusser did not address it; adherents are split.

workers-own-party.rationale: Althusser worked within the French Communist Party and defended its role as the party of the working class, with class struggle central.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the school's communist aim and class analysis, which opposes patriarchal family relations; the practice was not discussed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Althusser analyses the family as an ideological apparatus reproducing relations of production, so equal legal rights for women are inferred to be supported.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by the school; no principle clearly settles the question.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: private tort law belongs to the bourgeois legal apparatus, and a Marxist left prefers public regulation of capital.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: traditional authority is an ideological apparatus of pre-capitalist or capitalist reproduction, and a formal advisory role is unlikely to be welcomed.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; the school has no stated view on trading liberty against ecology, and adherents split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred: the judiciary and prisons are repressive state apparatuses, and the school is critical of harsher state punishment.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed by the school; adherents plausibly divide between integration and opposing compulsion.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from its class-struggle politics and PCF-aligned tradition: Marxists back strong unions, so compulsory-membership bans (right-to-work) are opposed.

voter-id.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the left's view of ID rules as barriers to working-class voting, though the school cares little for electoral detail.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the school's view of religion as an ideological state apparatus: no church should hold privileged state status, a secular-state position.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: It treats bourgeois democracy as the form of class rule, so electoral procedure alone does not make a state democratic.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a communist-left secular outlook that treats sexual morality as ideology rather than a binding norm.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its view of the repressive state apparatus as an instrument of class power; adherents would oppose it as bourgeois repression.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: a cash-substitute for welfare is a market-liberal scheme that dismantles collective provision, which a Marxist left rejects.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal political rights follow from the communist emancipatory aim and the PCF tradition, which backed women's suffrage.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Althusser classes religion as an ideological apparatus that reproduces class domination, but the school does not single it out as a major cause of women's oppression; it stresses capitalism and the family apparatus.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: the school treats categories as products of ideology and social structure, not natural facts.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: a left state tradition favours public institutions to address inequality, though the school stresses class over gender.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Marxism treats property as a social relation of production and rejects natural-rights claims to private ownership by first appropriation; Althusser's analysis of relations of production implies this.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the view that law and courts belong to the state's ideological and repressive apparatus serving the ruling class; not discussed.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Althusser treats religion as an ideological apparatus that interpellates subjects; literal inerrancy is not a view the school holds.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equality in the communist tradition; the school did not discuss Indigenous self-rule.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Althusser criticised the Stalinist bureaucracy and the 'cult of personality' yet stayed in the Communist Party defending socialist states; adherents are split.

indirect-election.rationale: Althusser's late essays criticised the party's abandonment of the dictatorship of the proletariat and Poulantzas favoured democratic socialism with councils alongside representation; split and inferred.

national-church-status.rationale: The school treats the Church as the dominant ideological state apparatus of precapitalist society, replaced by the school; a privileged national church is rejected.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed by the school, which focused on class structures; inferred as split.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; the school's focus on class makes it indifferent, and the Marxist tradition on self-determination is mixed.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic for a school focused on Western capitalist structures.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred; Marxism aims at abundance through developed productive forces, not voluntary limitation of needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed by the school; inferred as split.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from commitment to the equality of women and men within the communist tradition; conscription was not discussed.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Marxism is internationalist and treats national attachments as ideological; inferred from that tradition, not an Althusserian topic.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Althusser criticises Stalinist repression and defends a democratic road to socialism, so killing without trial contradicts the school's stated line.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed; Althusser's circle was sympathetic to Chinese Marxism but the PCF tradition gave no fixed geopolitical line.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Marxist internationalism, which gives no priority to ethnic kin abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist aim of social ownership of the means of production, though compensation to all is not an Althusserian formulation.

self-ownership.rationale: Althusser holds that individuals are constituted as subjects by ideology, so the self-owning autonomous individual is itself an ideological notion.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from a left-wing party's opposition to regressive indirect taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from the left tradition's preference for universal provision over means-tested aid.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Althusser's late essays keep the party central to class struggle and democratic socialism, so bypassing parties is rejected.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist view of the state serving capitalist interests, which Poulantzas analysed.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Althusser treats the church as an ideological state apparatus, so secular politics follows from the school's analysis.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: ancestral values would be treated as ideology rather than a goal; not addressed directly.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the left tradition, which sees family law as part of the ideological apparatuses and favours women's equality.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist left tradition, though the sources do not discuss resource sovereignty.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Marxists, Althusserians included, treat distribution as determined by relations of production rather than by the fairness of how holdings arose.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: Althusserians see finance as part of the capitalist structure and a leftist reform would be tolerated, but it is not discussed.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: structural Marxism makes class the determining structure, and racism would be treated as overdetermined by it rather than extinct.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: Althusser treats law as part of the state apparatus serving class rule, not as moral reasoning about bindingness.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the communist aim of ending exploitation; the question is not addressed by the school.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: the school opposes imperialism and the dominance of one capitalist centre, but did not address world order directly.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Reading Capital reinterprets rather than discards Marx's economics, and the school keeps the exploitation of labour as central.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from Althusser's internationalist class analysis; the PCF's patriotic line was not his emphasis.

material-over-identity.rationale: Class struggle is central to the school, but its focus on ideology gives culture real weight, so adherents are partly split.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Althusser criticised Soviet-style party rule at the 22nd Congress, and the sources do not address market socialism; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Ideology is a permanent feature of every society, including a communist one, because it shapes how people live their relation to the world.
missingStatements.rationale: Althusser holds ideology has no history and is essential to every society, a central thesis of the school.
missingStatements.declined: Thesis specific to Althusserian theory; few other ideologies take a side and the bank must stay lean.

missingStatements.text: Human beings are produced as subjects by the social structures and ideologies they live in, rather than being the makers of history.
missingStatements.rationale: History is a process without a subject and individuals are bearers of structures constituted as subjects by interpellation.

missingStatements.text: Schools, churches and families mainly serve to reproduce the existing relations of production.
missingStatements.rationale: Althusser names the school as the dominant ideological state apparatus of mature capitalism, replacing the Church.

notes: Poulantzas rejected instrumentalism and stressed the relative autonomy of the capitalist state; Althusser's own politics ran from PCF orthodoxy to criticism of the party in 1977-78. Positions on social and foreign-policy topics the school never discussed are inferences from its class analysis and the French communist milieu.
